column1: In the first and second millennia BCE, pirates sailed around the Mediterranean, attacking ships and avoiding pursuers
column2: 在公元前第一和第二个千年间，海盗们在地中海各处航行，袭击船只，躲避追兵。
column3: first and second millennia|第一和第二个千年

column1: When one mentions pirates, an image springs to most people’s minds of a crew of misfits, daredevils and adventurers in command of a tall sailing ship in the Caribbean Sea.
column2: 一提到海盗，多数人脑中就会浮现这样的画面：一群不合群的人、亡命之徒和冒险家，驾着一艘高大的帆船，航行在加勒比海上。
column4: springs to most people’s minds|浮现在多数人的脑海

column1: Yet from the first to the third millennium BCE, thousands of years before these swashbucklers began spreading fear across the Caribbean, pirates prowled the Mediterranean, raiding merchant ships and threatening vital trade routes.
column2: 然而，在公元前第一至第三个千年间，早在这些冒险之徒开始令加勒比海一带人心惶惶的几千年前，海盗就已经在地中海上四处游弋，劫掠商船，威胁重要的贸易航线了。

column1: However, despite all efforts and the might of various ancient states, piracy could not be stopped.
column2: 然而，尽管古代许多国家实力强大，也曾用尽办法，海盗活动还是没能被制止。

column1: The situation remained unchanged for thousands of years.
column2: 数千年来，局面一直如此。
column5: for thousands of years|历经数千年

column1: Only when the pirates directly threatened the interests of ancient Rome did the Roman Republic organise a massive fleet to eliminate piracy.
column2: 直到海盗直接威胁到古罗马的利益，罗马共和国才组织起一支庞大的舰队，以铲除海盗活动。

column1: Under the command of the Roman general Pompey, Rome eradicated piracy, transforming the Mediterranean into ‘Mare Nostrum’ (Our Sea).
column2: 在罗马将领庞培的指挥下，罗马根除了海盗活动，把地中海变成了“Mare Nostrum”，即“我们的海”。
column3: Under the command of|在……的指挥下
column8: Mare Nostrum|拉丁语，意为“我们的海”

column1: Although piracy in the Mediterranean is first recorded in ancient Egypt during the reign of Pharaoh Amenhotep III (c 1390-1353 BCE), it is reasonable to assume it predated this powerful civilisation.
column2: 关于地中海海盗的最早记载出现在古埃及法老阿蒙霍特普三世在位期间（约公元前1390年至前1353年），不过，有理由推测，海盗活动比这个强盛的文明还要古老。

column1: This is partly due to the great importance the Mediterranean held at this time, and partly due to its geography.
column2: 这既是因为地中海在当时有重要地位，也与其地理环境有关。

column1: While the Mediterranean region is predominantly fertile, some parts are rugged and hilly, even mountainous.
column2: 地中海地区的大部分土地虽然肥沃，但也有些地方崎岖多丘陵，有的甚至群山连绵。

column1: In the ancient times, the inhabitants of these areas relied heavily on marine resources, including fish and salt.
column2: 古时，这些地区的居民十分依赖鱼、盐等海洋资源。

column1: Most had their own boats, possessed good seafaring skills, and unsurpassed knowledge of the local coastline and sailing routes.
column2: 他们大多有自己的船，航海技术娴熟，对当地海岸线和航线的了解也无人能及。

column1: Thus, it is not surprising that during hardships, these men turned to piracy.
column2: 因此，遇上艰困的日子，这些人转而当海盗也就不足为奇了。

column1: Geography itself further benefited the pirates, with the numerous coves along the coast providing places for them to hide their boats and strike undetected.
column2: 地理环境本身也给了海盗更多便利。沿岸众多的小海湾既能藏船，也能让他们在不被察觉的情况下出击。

column1: Before the invention of ocean-going caravels* in the 15th century, ships could not easily cross long distances over open water.
column2: 在15世纪远洋卡拉维尔帆船发明之前，船只很难在无遮蔽的开阔水域长距离航行。
column5: caravels|n. 卡拉维尔帆船，葡萄牙人研制的小型灵便帆船
column6: cross long distances|跨越很长的距离

column1: Thus, in the ancient world most were restricted to a few well-known navigable routes that followed the coastline.
column2: 因此，在古代，大多数船只能沿着海岸的几条人们熟知的通航路线行驶。
column8: followed the coastline|沿海岸线延伸

column1: Caught in a trap, a slow merchant ship laden with goods had no other option but to surrender.
column2: 一旦落入圈套，满载货物、行驶缓慢的商船就只能投降。
column3: Caught in a trap|落入圈套
column7: no other option but to|除……之外别无选择

column1: In addition, knowledge of the local area helped the pirates to avoid retaliation once a state fleet arrived.
column2: 此外，一旦某国舰队赶来，海盗凭借对当地的熟悉也能躲过报复。

column1: One should also add that it was not unknown in the first and second millennia BCE for governments to resort to pirates’ services, especially during wartime, employing their skills and numbers against their opponents.
column2: 还要补充一点：在公元前第一和第二个千年间，政府借助海盗的力量，也并非没有先例。尤其是在战时，政府会利用海盗的技能和人数来对付敌方。

column1: A pirate fleet would serve in the first wave of attack, preparing the way for the navy.
column2: 海盗舰队会参加第一波进攻，为海军开路。
column5: first wave of attack|n. 第一波进攻

column1: Some of the regions were known for providing safe harbours to pirates, who, in return, boosted the local economy.
column2: 当时有些地区以向海盗提供安全港湾而闻名，海盗反过来也带动了当地经济。

column1: The first known record of a named group of Mediterranean pirates, made during the rule of ancient Egyptian Pharaoh Akhenaten (c 1353-1336 BCE), was in the Amarna Letters.
column2: 已知最早一份明确写出某个地中海海盗群体名称的记载，出自《阿玛尔纳书信》，记于古埃及法老阿肯那顿在位时期（约公元前1353年至前1336年）。
column3: first known record|n. 已知最早的记载
column4: named group|n. 有明确名称的群体
column5: during the rule of|在……统治期间

column1: These were extracts of diplomatic correspondence between the pharaoh and his allies, and covered many pressing issues, including piracy.
column2: 这些书信是法老与盟友之间外交通信的节选，内容涉及包括海盗活动在内的许多紧迫问题。

column1: It seems the pharaoh was troubled by two distinct pirate groups, the Lukka and the Sherden.
column2: 法老似乎受到两个不同海盗群体的困扰，它们分别是卢卡人和谢尔登人。
column6: distinct|adj. 不同的；各自独立的

column1: Despite the Egyptian fleet’s best efforts, the pirates continued to cause substantial disruption to regional commerce.
column2: 尽管埃及舰队竭尽全力，海盗仍不断给地区贸易造成严重干扰。

column1: In the letters, the king of Alashiya (modern Cyprus) rejected Akhenaten’s claims of a connection with the Lukka (based in modern-day Turkey).
column2: 在信中，阿拉希亚（今塞浦路斯）的国王否认了阿肯那顿关于他与卢卡人有联系的说法。卢卡人的据点位于今天的土耳其境内。

column1: The king assured Akhenaten he was prepared to punish any of his subjects involved in piracy.
column2: 这位国王向阿肯那顿保证，凡是参与海盗活动的臣民，他都愿意惩处。

column1: The ancient Greek world’s experience of piracy was different from that of Egyptian rulers.
column2: 古希腊世界对海盗活动的体验，与埃及统治者的经历不同。

column1: While Egypt’s power was land-based, the ancient Greeks relied on the Mediterranean in almost all aspects of life, from trade to warfare.
column2: 埃及的实力以陆地为根基，而古希腊人生活中的几乎所有方面，从贸易到战争，都依赖地中海。

column1: Interestingly, in his works the Iliad and the Odyssey, the ancient Greek writer Homer not only condones, but praises the lifestyle and actions of pirates.
column2: 有意思的是，古希腊作家荷马在《伊利亚特》和《奥德赛》中，对海盗的生活方式和行为不但予以容忍，而且加以赞美。

column1: The opinion remained unchanged in the following centuries.
column2: 在随后的几个世纪里，这种看法一直没有改变。

column1: The ancient Greek historian Thucydides, for instance, glorified pirates’ daring attacks on ships or even cities.
column2: 例如，古希腊历史学家修昔底德颂扬过海盗对船只、甚至对城市发起的大胆袭击。

column1: For Greeks, piracy was a part of everyday life.
column2: 对希腊人来说，海盗活动是日常生活的一部分。

column1: Even high-ranking members of the state were not beyond engaging in such activities.
column2: 就连国家的高级官员也会参与这类活动。
column6: not beyond engaging in|也会参与；并非不屑于做

column1: According to the Greek orator Demosthenes, in 355 BCE, Athenian ambassadors made a detour from their official travel to capture a ship sailing from Egypt, taking the wealth found onboard for themselves!
column2: 据希腊演说家德摩斯梯尼记述，公元前355年，雅典的使节们在执行公务途中绕道截获了一艘从埃及驶来的船，还把船上的财物据为己有！

column1: The Greeks’ liberal approach towards piracy does not mean they always tolerated it, but attempts to curtail piracy were hampered by the large number of pirates operating in the Mediterranean.
column2: 希腊人对海盗活动态度宽松，并不意味着他们总会容忍海盗。不过，由于活跃在地中海的海盗人数众多，遏制海盗活动的努力受到了阻碍。

column1: The rising power of ancient Rome required the Roman Republic to deal with piracy in the Mediterranean.
column2: 随着古罗马实力增强，罗马共和国必须应对地中海上的海盗活动。
column3: rising power|n. 日益增强的实力

column1: While piracy was a serious issue for the Republic, Rome profited greatly from its existence.
column2: 海盗活动虽是共和国面临的一个严重问题，罗马却也从它的存在中获益颇丰。
column6: profited greatly from|从……中获益颇丰

column1: Pirate raids provided a steady source of slaves, essential for Rome’s agriculture and mining industries.
column2: 海盗的劫掠为罗马提供了稳定的奴隶来源，而奴隶对罗马的农业和采矿业至关重要。

column1: But this arrangement could work only while the pirates left Roman interests alone.
column2: 但只有海盗不触碰罗马的利益，这种局面才维持得下去。
column6: left Roman interests alone|不侵犯罗马的利益

column1: Pirate attacks on grain ships, which were essential to Roman citizens, led to angry voices in the Senate, demanding punishment of the culprits.
column2: 运粮船对罗马民众至关重要。海盗袭击运粮船，在元老院引起了愤怒的声讨，人们要求惩罚肇事者。

column1: Rome, however, did nothing, further encouraging piracy.
column2: 然而，罗马没有采取任何行动，这进一步助长了海盗活动。

column1: By the 1st century BCE, emboldened pirates kidnapped prominent Roman dignitaries, asking for a large ransom to be paid.
column2: 到公元前一世纪，越来越大胆的海盗绑架罗马显贵，索要高额赎金。
column3: By the 1st century BCE|到公元前一世纪

column1: Their most famous hostage was none other than Julius Caesar, captured in 75 BCE.
column2: 他们最有名的人质不是别人，正是在公元前75年被俘的尤利乌斯·恺撒。
column4: none other than|不是别人，正是
column5: Julius Caesar|n. 尤利乌斯·恺撒

column1: By now, Rome was well aware that pirates had outlived their usefulness.
column2: 至此，罗马已经十分清楚，海盗已不再有利用价值。
column5: outlived their usefulness|已失去利用价值

column1: The time had come for concerted action.
column2: 采取协同行动的时候到了。
column3: the time had come|时机已经到来

column1: In 67 BCE, a new law granted Pompey vast funds to combat the Mediterranean menace.
column2: 公元前67年，一项新法律拨给庞培巨额资金，以对付地中海上的这股威胁。

column1: Taking personal command, Pompey divided the entire Mediterranean into 13 districts, assigning a fleet and commander to each.
column2: 庞培亲自指挥，把整个地中海划分为13个区域，每个区域都配有一支舰队和一名指挥官。

column1: After cleansing one district of pirates, the fleet would join another in the next district.
column2: 每清除一个区域的海盗，该舰队就会前往下一个区域，与当地的另一支舰队会合。

column1: The process continued until the entire Mediterranean was free of pirates.
column2: 这一过程持续进行，直到整个地中海再没有海盗。

column1: Although thousands of pirates died at the hands of Pompey’s troops, as a long-term solution to the problem, many more were offered land in fertile areas located far from the sea.
column2: 尽管有数千名海盗死于庞培的军队之手，但作为解决问题的长远办法，更多的海盗得到了分配给他们的土地，这些土地位于远离海洋的肥沃地区。
column3: at the hands of|死于……之手；遭……所为
column5: long-term solution|n. 长远的解决办法

column1: Instead of a maritime menace, Rome got productive farmers that further boosted its economy.
column2: 昔日威胁海上安全的海盗成了从事农业生产的农民，进一步带动了罗马的经济。
